title: Executive Director, Sustainability Planning & Strategy, Asia Pacific Division (APD) - SMBC
description:
**Company Overview**

* Headquartered in Tokyo, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) is a leading global financial institution and a core member of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMBC Group). Built upon our rich Japanese heritage since 1876, we put our customers first and provide seamless access to, from and within the Asia Pacific region. SMBC is one of the largest Japanese banks by assets and maintains strong credit ratings across our global integrated network. We work closely as one SMBC Group to offer personal, corporate and investment banking services to meet the needs of our customers.
* With sustainability embedded within our strategy and operations as Social Value Creation , we are committed to creating a society in which today's generation can enjoy economic prosperity and well-being and pass it on to future generations.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Develop and further drive the agenda of APD wide sustainability mindset and culture aligned with the organization's mission and values.
* Leading and organise a team of sustainability professionals to effectively deliver agreed strategy.
* Oversee strategy implementation by the team, ensuring regular cadence between the team and Heads of Countries and Heads of BUs from a policy and engagement point
* Managing Responsible Financing and sustainability risk policies of the Bank, including developing new policies for identifying, managing, and monitoring environmental and social risks, and ensuring relevance and effective in building firm-wide resilience to sustainability risks, as well as compliance with relevant regulations and aligned with industry standards
* Work with Deputy Head of APD who is in charge of Sustainability in the region and the office of Global Chief Sustainability Officer (CS u O) in Head office to serve as a point of contact for engagements with regulators, governmental agencies, industry associations, NGOs and other relevant agencies/bodies on sustainability matters and where required, collaborate with internal stakeholders to ensure appropriate responses and communications
* Governance and Reporting by working with stakeholders to organise and structure information for various sustainability reporting. Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) for sustainability and regularly report progress to Senior Management team and relevant stakeholders
* Ensure transparent and accurate reporting on sustainability metrics in alignment with industry standards
* Working cross-functionally with bank-wide stakeholders to define and drive the implementation of frameworks, policies, and tools, and facilitate various programmes and initiatives enabling effective sustainability capability development and risk management across the Bank
* Driving a collaborative, cross-functional team towards establishing sustainability understanding, practices and application of selected international standards/guidelines across the bank
* Engaging subsidiaries to ensure prompt adoption and localisation of the Group sustainability policies and to ensure compliance with Group core standards
* Facilitating awareness and capacity building on sustainability and risk management

**Key Attributes and Skills**

* At least 15-20 years of proven leadership track record and expertise in franchise-building, corporate client-facing role in the areas of sustainability/climate advisory, and/or environmental and social consulting
* Relevant academic studies will be advantageous in sustainability, environmental science, environmental engineering and development
* Demonstrates experience and ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders externally and internally in the area of sustainability-related matters
* Possesses a broad and deep network of senior relationships within this scope and relevant industry sectors
* In-depth knowledge of key sustainability issues, sustainability international standards/principles, relevant regulations & standards, and best practices relevanc e to the banking sector
* Familiar with international environmental and social policies, procedures, and standards such as IFC performance standards and/or GHG Protocol and possessing in-depth environmental and social due diligence experience
* Proficient in project management with strong analytical skills in analyzing data and identifying trends to understand data systems

title: Sr. Environmental & Social Risk Advisor, Singapore
description:
As an Export Credit Agency, Export Development Canada (EDC) helps Canadian companies of all sizes succeed on the world stage. With this goal in mind, EDC aims to increase trade opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region through growing our local presence in Singapore with a variety of locally-offered services.
  
  
The EDC branch office in Singapore serves as a hub for the Asia-Pacific region. The branch allows us to support our Asia-Pacific and Canadian customers more effectively as they go, grow and succeed internationally.
  
  
At EDC, we view Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) as a competitive advantage for ourselves and our customers. Through our deep subject matter expertise, we support organizations of all sizes to evolve their responsible business practices as a means of improving their competitive position. Most of our Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) team resides in Canada, but we have a Singapore team that is expanding to accelerate the impact we can have in the Asia-Pacific region through local expertise and timely support.
  
  
Job Overview
  
  
The EDC Singapore branch office is seeking a motivated and resourceful person to join our ESRM team as an Senior Environmental and Social (E&S) Risk Advisor for the Asia-Pacific region. The ESRM team is responsible for helping fulfill EDC's commitments to conduct business in a responsible and ethical manner and integrate our ESG values into the business we do. The Senior E&S Risk Advisor will be responsible for conducting due diligence on the business we support for our customers doing business or looking to expand into the Asia-Pacific region. Our vision for this role is to be an integral part of the business team to help manage relationships with our customers and partners and guide them on their ESG journey and ensure this journey is reflective of the E&S risks in their business. The role will be supported through close collaboration with the head office in Ottawa.
  
  
This is an opportunity for an individual who is a resourceful E&S risk analyst, who can form strong relationships with EDC clients in the Asia-Pacific region, EDC business teams and ESRM colleagues, whether based in Singapore, the Asia-Pacific region or Canada and who thrives in a dynamic environment.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
Leads the assessment of EDC transactions, identifying material E&S risks and recommending key mitigants for EDC's financing transactions. Applies the Equator Principles, the IFC Performance Standards, the UNGPs and other international standards as relevant.
  
  
Analyzes and determines the adequacy of ESIAs, ESDD reports, monitoring reports, thematic reports (e.g., biodiversity, archeology, human rights), environmental and social action plans (ESAPs), audit reports, consultant terms of reference, request for proposals, E&S-related policies with the aim of managing E&S risks and promoting alignment with good practice and international standards
  
  
In collaboration with EDC business teams, negotiates with EDC clients the incorporation of E&S commitments in financing documentation to prevent, mitigate, or address the E&S risks on EDC's commercial transactions
  
  
Manages relationships with diverse stakeholders, including internal and external clients, co-lending IFIs, DFIs, and ECAs and consultants, building high levels of professional credibility and mutual trust
  
  
Undertakes site visits, assessing E&S capacity and performance in the field within the Asia-Pacific Region (typical 1-6 days, 1-5 times per year)
  
  
Monitors transaction / project performance over time, identifying and resolving issues of non-compliance with E&S commitments.
  
  
As a subject matter expert, advises management and senior management on a range of E&S issues, including those prevalent in the Asia-Pacific Region, making authoritative technical and professional recommendations to improve the improve the E&S performance of EDC's transactions.
  
  
Produces and/or edit documents in line with organizational-style guidelines and prepares information for consumption by EDC risk management committees, business teams, senior management and/or external clients
  
  
Provide specialist advice on the interpretation and application of ESRM policies, procedures, programs and/or products to EDC underwriting teams, business teams and others, to resolve complex or contentious queries and issues and enable others to take appropriate actions
  
  
Maintain and renew a deep knowledge and understanding of the organization's ESRM policies and procedures and of relevant regulatory codes and codes of conduct, and ensure transactions adhere to required standards.
  
  
Develop an understanding of EDC's mandate, Asia-Pacific strategic focus and financing products, and identify opportunities to advance the sustainability agenda with clients in the region.
  
  
Occasionally support EDC on non-transactional E&S-related interactions with relevant external stakeholders
  
  
What We Are Looking For
  
  
Completion of a degree in environmental or social sciences or in a sub-discipline such as ecology, environmental management, environmental and social risk management, climate change, biodiversity, water resources, international development, sustainable development, human rights, gender studies, occupational health and safety, community relations & resettlement, law (environmental or human rights) or engineering.
  
  
Advanced knowledge in ESIA and/or due diligence principles, frameworks and standards, including the Equator Principles and the IFC Performance Standards
  
  
Excellent communication and demonstrated ability to manage relationships with customers and stakeholders
  
  
Minimum of 7-10 years' experience in ESIA or ESDD in the consulting space or equivalent industry experience within EDC-relevant business sectors (e.g. Extractive Industries, Agrifoods, Advance Manufacturing, Clean Tech and Renewable Energy, Apparel, utilities and Infrastructure)
  
  
Evidence of success in prioritizing and meeting deadlines in an environment that requires managing multiple competing tasks and responsibilities.
  
  
Evidence of ability to discern, distill, and concisely and clearly communicate (written and verbally) key issues in complex business transactions and provide advice based on client needs
  
  
Fluent in English for oral communication as well as reading and writing
  
  
Ability and willingness to travel up to 20% of working hours
  
  
Ability to work independently and collaboratively across geographies and time zones.
  
  
What Will Make You Stand Out
  
  
Expertise in social impact assessment or biodiversity impact assessment.
  
  
Experience working as an independent E&S consultant on behalf of lenders or in the financial services industry, on behalf of private sector companies in major project development or working at or with international finance institutions (Financial Institutions abiding to Equator Principles, Export Credit Agencies, Development Finance Institutions, Multilateral Development Banks)
  
  
In addition to English, can communicate in one or more local Asia-Pacific language
  
  
Degree, diploma or training in Business, Finance, or related disciplines
  
  
Export Development Canada (EDC) is a Crown corporation dedicated to helping Canadian companies of all sizes succeed on the world stage. We equip them with the tools they need – the trade knowledge, financial solutions, equity, insurance, and connections – to grow their business with confidence. This in turn, creates jobs and increases prosperity at home.
  
  
As international risk experts, we help Canadian companies to navigate, manage and take on risk to support their growth beyond Canada’s borders. Since 1944, businesses of all sizes and sectors have counted on us for the export knowledge and financial solutions they need to succeed in global markets. Beyond our solutions, we believe that sustainable, responsible and inclusive trade is a powerful force for good in Canada and around the world, and that’s what drives us.
  
  
**Our solutions include:**  
Capital – access to working capital and financing
  
  
Risk mitigation – insurance that lowers the risk of doing business abroad
  
  
Trade knowledge – expertise to help companies make informed decisions
  
  
Global connections – relationships that connect Canadian and international companies and help both parties grow
  
  
International Footprint
  
  
With offices across Canada and around the world, we are close to the Canadian businesses we support and to the buyers in global markets that can connect Canadian exporters to international supply chains.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility Executive
description:
The Corporate Social Responsibility Executive is responsible for managing the Company’s CSR initiatives and supporting the Corporate Affairs Team on events and communication.
  
  
A summary of the responsibilities of this position are, and not limited to, as follows:
  
  
Evaluate incoming sponsorship proposals for management review.
  
  
Plan and organize fundraising initiatives through collaborating with internal stakeholders, business partners and Non-Profit Organizations (NPO) including sourcing, liaising and executing fundraising events with multiple vendors.
  
  
Work with NPOs to curate a calendar of volunteering activities for staff on corporate, department and project levels
  
  
Manage and execute the marketing and communications of CSR initiatives through emails, Intranet and other outreach platforms.
  
  
Manage the sign-ups of supported charity sports and charity events involving staff participation and coordinate with the NPO.
  
  
Manage and maintain a good tracking system for CSR data for management reporting
  
  
Conduct annual surveys with internal stakeholders to identify employee interest and alignment with CSR initiatives.
  
  
Adherence to safety practices in the workplace.
  
  
Able to review and improve the various work processes to enhance execution efficiency.
  
  
Value Add of Position
  
  
Able to review and improve the various work processes to enhance execution efficiency
  
  
Qualifications and Requirements
  
  
**Education:** Diploma in Marketing/Communications, Sustainability, Hospitality, or other relevant field of study
  
  
**Experience:** Min 1 year of progressive experience
  
  
Independent and a self-starter, with strong personal drive to initiate and implement.
  
  
WOH HUP (PRIVATE) LIMITED
  
  
Established in 1927, Woh Hup began humbly as a one-man business in Malaya. Today, we are Singapore’s largest privately owned construction and civil engineering specialist, with a dedicated 1,000-strong workforce, and a body of work spanning many of Singapore’s most notable and iconic developments.
  
  
At the heart of our four-generation family-run business lies a proud heritage of industry, integrity and enterprise, focused on creating lasting value for our clients, improving quality and safety standards on every project, and maximising opportunities for our employees to achieve their career potential. These values have fueled the company’s growth consistently for more than 80 years, and continue to do so.
  
  
In our efforts to continuously raise the industry bar, we seek to introduce innovative new building solutions and broaden our skills through strategic joint-venture partnerships with overseas counterparts. This has seen us emerge in recent years from being a principal player in the building of private residential and commercial developments, to becoming a leader too in large-scale civil engineering works, cementing our position at the forefront of the construction industry, locally and regionally.

description:
**About Us**

CapitaLand Group (CapitaLand) is one of Asia’s largest diversified real estate groups. Headquartered in Singapore, CapitaLand’s portfolio focuses on real estate investment management and real estate development, and spans across more than 270 cities in over 45 countries.

**Job Description**

This internship provides a unique opportunity to work with the sustainability team at CapitaLand Development (CLD), alongside external industry experts. You will gain hands-on experience in emissions data analysis, market benchmark development, and sustainability reporting.

You will be tasked with analysing environmental data and conducting research for technical projects that directly influence CLD's emissions management practices and sustainability strategies. This includes working on low-carbon material solutions and learning about the decarbonization of the real estate and construction sector. This role is perfect for someone passionate about contributing to real-world sustainability initiatives and making a tangible impact.

**What You Will Get to Do**

**Contribute to Sustainability Projects**

* Support cross-functional teams on sustainability initiatives, such as ongoing decarbonization projects, green building certifications, and ESG reporting
* Assist in tracking progress on CLD’s sustainability goals and preparing reports on ESG key performance indicators (KPIs)
* Participate in internal sustainability workshops, helping to drive cultural change across the organization

**Research and Data Collection**

* Conduct research on the availability and nature of emissions data for concrete and its constituents in Singapore
* Compare emissions data with other regions, regionally and internationally, to identify gaps and opportunities for improvement
* Collaborate with stakeholders to collect and validate data for reporting purposes

**Support for Benchmark Development:**

* Assist in the creation of a tailored market benchmark for Singapore based on data collected during the reporting pilot
* Work closely with technical experts to validate methodologies and ensure accurate reporting

**What We Are Looking For**

* Preferred a Master student or as part of Doctorate thesis
* Enrolled in a degree program related to sustainability, sustainable design, environmental science, engineering, or a related field
* Strong analytical skills with an interest in sustainability data and reporting
* Knowledge of excel and similar tools for data collection and processing
* Good communication skills, with the ability to work in a collaborative environment
* Knowledge of carbon accounting or emissions reporting methodologies is an advantage but not required

**Closing Statement:**

At CapitaLand, we advocate fair employment practices, and recruit talents based on merit and fit with our Corporate values. We provide equal opportunity for all qualified persons and build an inclusive workplace regardless of race, gender, age, religious belief or nationality.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.
